method: Using the previously measured candidate radial bands and independently estimated angular phases, sample image-gradient evidence along each candidate wedge's left/right angular walls and inner/outer radial boundaries. Compare mean boundary evidence with wedge-interior gradient evidence. This tests local enclosure tendency; it does not by itself prove a planar cell.

families.interpretation: All three candidate wedges show aggregate enclosure evidence, but this does not resolve the previously ambiguous third angular boundary; treat as supportive screening only.

Aggregate boundary evidence is generally above interior evidence, but only 2/7 wedges satisfy the strict all-four-boundaries criterion. Several radial closures are weak; 7-fold periodicity remains stronger evidence than closed-cell count.

Most wedges have aggregate boundary evidence above their interiors, but only 4/12 pass the strict all-four-boundaries criterion. 12-fold periodicity is not yet equivalent to 12 independently closed planar cells.

adjudication.reason: Independent 3/7/12 periodicity is supported at different radial scales and local enclosure tendency is present, but strict closed-cell evidence is heterogeneous, especially for 7- and 12-fold bands.

methodologicalConsequence: Do not create 22 CR-MF identities yet. The next pass must trace connected boundary curves / planar faces rather than assume radial wedges are cells.
